response: Pictorial warning labels (HWLs) on cigarette packages can potentially address smoking-related health disparities, particularly when combined with didactic textual forms. Research suggests that HWLs with this type of content may be more effective than those with testimonial narratives. However, further studies are needed to determine which pictorial HWL content has the greatest real-world impact among consumers from disadvantaged groups. Additionally, it is essential to assess how HWL content should change to maintain its impact as tobacco control environments strengthen and consumer awareness of smoking-related risks increases. This is crucial in reducing health disparities, especially among vulnerable populations, such as those exposed to secondhand smoke, including infants discharged from NICUs, who are at a higher risk of tobacco exposure and subsequent tobacco-related health disparities.
